chunks: 12 – Sulaymān b. ʿUmar, Abū Dāwud, al-Nakhaʿī. Narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Mūsā narrated to me, he said: Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Saʿīd narrated to me, he said: The muḥaddiths used to nickname Abū Dāwud al-Nakhaʿī: "the liar of al-Nakhaʿ".

key_terms.أَبُو دَاوُدَ: Abu Dawud, a kunya (nominal epithet) used for Sulayman ibn Umar.
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.النَّخَعِيُّ: Al-Nakha'i, a nisba indicating origin from the region of al-Nakha.
key_terms.الْمُحَدِّثُونَ: The muhaddithun, scholars of hadith and narrators.
key_terms.كَذَّابُ النَّخَعِ: The liar of al-Nakha, a nickname given to Sulman ibn Umar by scholars.

ai.seo_question: Who was Sulayman ibn Umar al-Nakha'i and why was he called the liar of al-Nakha?
ai.summary: This biographical entry from the book of narrators (Kitab al-Du'afa) identifies Sulaymān ibn ʿUmar, known as Abū Dāwud al-Nakhaʿī, as a narrator of the Imams. It records that the scholars of hadith (muḥaddithūn) nicknamed him "the liar of al-Nakhaʿ," indicating a specific criticism of his reliability or truthfulness in narration.
